saints.name: The Conversion of St. Paul
saints.title: Feast of the Apostle
saints.shortBlurb: The day the fiercest persecutor of the Church was struck down on the Damascus road and made an apostle…
biography: Saul of Tarsus, a Pharisee who had approved the stoning of Stephen and still breathed threats against the disciples, set out for Damascus with letters from the high priest to arrest the followers of Jesus. As the Acts of the Apostles recounts, a light from heaven threw him to the ground, and the voice of the risen Christ asked, 'Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?'

Blinded, he was led into the city, where for three days he neither ate nor drank until the disciple Ananias laid hands on him; something like scales fell from his eyes, and he rose from the waters of baptism the apostle of the Gentiles. He himself retold the event in Acts before the Jerusalem crowd and before King Agrippa.

From that hour his journeys and letters carried the Gospel across the Roman world, until he sealed his preaching by martyrdom at Rome under Nero. The Church has kept this feast of his conversion on 25 January since at least the eighth century; it closes the Week of Prayer for Christian Unity, observed each year since 1908.
saints.knownFor: His conversion from persecutor to Apostle of the Gentiles.
